status_summary: Two bipartisan bills introduced in 2025 would direct the FCC to complete a rulemaking within 18 months of enactment that adds broadband providers and edge providers (platforms, search, streaming, app stores, cloud and similar services) to the Universal Service Fund contribution base: S. 1651 (introduced 2025-05-07, referred to Senate Commerce) and H.R. 4032 (introduced 2025-06-17, referred to House Energy and Commerce). Both exempt edge providers that carry under 3 percent of U.S. broadband traffic and earn under 5 billion dollars in U.S. revenue. A Congressional Research Service product dated 2026-07-30 describes them as introduced only, and no committee action was found. The FCC has not changed the contribution base; its 2026 universal service proposals cover Lifeline, high-cost support, E-Rate and fund administration, and the Supreme Court upheld the existing funding mechanism on 2025-06-27.

timeline.event: S. 1651, the Lowering Broadband Costs for Consumers Act of 2025 (Sen. Mullin with Sens. Kelly, Crapo and Cramer), is introduced and referred to the Senate Commerce Committee; it would require an FCC rulemaking to expand USF contributions to broadband providers and edge providers.
H.R. 4032, a companion bill with the same title (Rep. Feenstra, with bipartisan cosponsors), is introduced in the House and referred to Energy and Commerce.

Supreme Court decides FCC v. Consumers' Research (Nos. 24-354 and 24-422), 6 to 3, reversing the Fifth Circuit and holding that the universal service contribution scheme violates neither the nondelegation doctrine nor the private nondelegation doctrine, leaving the USF funding structure in place.
FCC proposed rule on Lifeline and Link Up reform published in the Federal Register (context: program design, not the contribution base).
FCC proposed rule on reforming the high-cost program published (context: program design, not the contribution base).

Congressional Research Service reports that edge providers and broadband internet access providers do not contribute to the USF, that the contribution factor reached 37.0 percent in the second quarter of 2026, and that S. 1651 and H.R. 4032 have been introduced; it describes a long-pending FCC contribution reform proceeding that lists broadband revenue as an option.
FCC proposal to review the E-Rate program published (context: program design, not the contribution base).

FCC proposed rule on universal service administration published (WC Docket 26-173; comments due 2026-09-30, replies 2026-10-30); it covers USAC processes, audits and board size and does not address who contributes or the contribution factor.
